description: An evolution strategy (ES) minimises a function of real variables with a population of μ parents. Each of λ children mixes ρ parents (*recombination*), changes its own step sizes by a random log-normal factor, and then adds Gaussian noise with those step sizes. With comma selection, (μ/ρ,λ), the μ best children become the next parents; with plus selection, (μ/ρ+λ), parents and children compete together, so the best point is never lost. Because each child carries its step sizes, good step sizes survive with good points (*self-adaptation*); one step size per coordinate copes with badly scaled problems. Use it for continuous problems without gradients; it is a heuristic with no optimality guarantee.
